info.title: IPGeolocation.io: Abuse Contact API
info.description:
Retrieve abuse contact information associated with an IPv4 address or IPv6 address.
The API returns the organization responsible for handling abuse complaints related
to the queried IP address, including the abuse contact name and kind, organization name,
registered address, email contacts, and phone numbers.

The abuse contact data helps organizations report malicious activities such as
spam, phishing, DDoS attacks, IP spoofing, and other network abuse to the
responsible network operator.

Two endpoints are available:

- **Single lookup** (`GET /v3/abuse`) returns abuse contact information for a
  single IPv4 or IPv6 address per request.
- **Bulk lookup** (`POST /v3/abuse-bulk`) accepts up to 50,000 IPs in a
  single request.

Both endpoints support the `fields`, `excludes` and `output` parameters to
control which fields are returned and reduce payload size when only specific
data is required.

## Authentication

Two authentication methods are supported:

### API Key

Pass your API key as the `apiKey` query parameter on every request. You can find your
key in the [IPGeolocation dashboard](https://app.ipgeolocation.io/). Store it in
server-side environment variables. Avoid exposing it in client-side JavaScript.

### Request Origin (CORS)

Available on paid plans only. Whitelist your domain in the dashboard under the
"API Keys" section. Once configured, requests from that domain (and all its subdomains)
are accepted without passing `apiKey`. Enter your root domain (e.g. `example.com`),
not the full URL. Bulk requests (`POST /v3/abuse-bulk`) always require an `apiKey`.

Each plan has a limit on the number of extra API keys and request origins:

| Plan | Extra API Keys + Request Origins |
|---|---|
| Free | 0 |
| Starter | 1 |
| Plus | 2 |
| Pro | 2 |
| Business | 3 |
| Premium | 3 |

Plans are sized by API credits, not requests: Free includes 1,000 credits
per day; Starter 150,000 credits/month; Plus 500,000; Pro 1,000,000;
Business 2,000,000; Premium 5,000,000.

Additional keys or origins can be added for $2.50 per month each.

## Response Formats

The API supports JSON (default) and XML output.

- Set the `output` query parameter to `json` or `xml`.
- Alternatively, set the `Accept` header to `application/json`, `application/xml`,
  or `text/xml`.

If neither is specified, the response is returned as JSON. If both are set, the
`Accept` header takes precedence for successful responses and authentication errors
(see the `output` parameter). Single lookup XML responses use a
`LinkedHashMap` root element; bulk XML responses use an `ArrayList` root with
one `item` element per entry.

## Credit Usage

Credits are charged only for successful **HTTP 200** responses. The exact number of
credits consumed by a request is returned in the `X-Credits-Charged` response header.

A **single IP abuse contact lookup** (`GET /v3/abuse`) consumes **1 credit** per request.
For **bulk lookups** (`POST /v3/abuse-bulk`), **1 credit is charged for each IP that
returns abuse contact data**.

For bulk requests, the total credits charged equal the number of IPs that return
abuse contact data multiplied by the per-IP credit cost. Entries returned as a
`message` object (malformed, empty, null, private or bogon IPs, and IPs with no
abuse contact in the database) do not consume credits.

## Field Filtering

Use `fields` to cherry-pick specific fields, or `excludes` to drop fields you do not
need. Both accept dot-notation for nested fields (e.g. `abuse.route`,
`abuse.organization`). The `ip` field is always present regardless of filters.

## Parameter Name Casing

Query parameter names are case-sensitive. Use exact names such as
`apiKey`, `ip`, `fields`, `excludes`, and `output`.

## Plan Availability and Usage Limits

The IP Abuse Contact API is available **only on paid plans** and costs
**1 credit** per successful lookup (bulk: 1 credit per IP that returns abuse
contact data).

Billing is based on API credits, not requests. Each billing period includes a
fixed credit allowance. After the allowance is exhausted, requests continue
only while overage (surcharge) is enabled and within its limit; otherwise the
API returns HTTP 429.

Free plans cannot access the IP Abuse Contact API. Requests made with a free plan API key return **HTTP 401 Unauthorized**.

get.description:
Returns abuse contact information for a single IPv4 or IPv6 address.

The response includes the organization responsible for handling abuse
complaints related to the queried IP address. This typically contains
the abuse contact name and kind, organization name, contact emails, phone
numbers, and the registered address.

This endpoint is intended for reporting malicious activities such as
spam, phishing, DDoS attacks, and other network abuse.

When only abuse contact information is required, using this endpoint is
recommended instead of `/v3/ipgeo?include=abuse` because it returns a
smaller response payload and predictable credit usage.

Each successful lookup consumes **1 credit**.

Use the `fields` and `excludes` parameters to control which parts of
the response are returned.

200.description: Abuse contact information for the requested IP address.

X-Credits-Charged.description: Number of API credits consumed by this request.

abuse.name: IRT-APNICRANDNET-AU
abuse.address: PO Box 3646, South Brisbane, QLD 4101, Australia

post.description:
Returns abuse contact information for up to **50,000 IPv4 or IPv6
addresses** in a single request.

The request body must contain an `ips` array.

Each IP is processed independently, and surrounding spaces are trimmed. Invalid,
empty, null, bogon, or private entries, and IPs with no abuse contact in the
database, return an object containing only a `message` field; the rest of the
request still succeeds.

Credits are charged **per IP that returns abuse contact data**, using the same
pricing as the single lookup endpoint (1 credit per IP).

When the number of entries that returned abuse contact data is lower than the
number of submitted entries, the response header `X-Successful-Record` gives
that number.

Bulk requests require an `apiKey`; they cannot be authenticated using Request
Origin alone.

Only the `POST` method is supported for this endpoint.

requestBody.description:
A JSON object containing an `ips` array. Each element is a string representing
an IPv4 address or IPv6 address. The array must not be empty and
must not contain more than 50,000 entries.

200.description:
An array of results, one per input IP address, in the same order as the
request `ips` array.

Successful entries return an abuse contact lookup object containing the IP
address and its abuse contact information.

Invalid, empty, null, private, or bogon entries, and IPs with no abuse contact
in the database, return an object containing only a `message` field; the rest
of the request still succeeds.

The `X-Successful-Record` response header is returned only when the number
of entries that returned abuse contact data is lower than the number of
submitted entries, and gives that number.

X-Credits-Charged.description:
Total number of API credits consumed. Equals 1 credit multiplied by the
count of IPs that returned abuse contact data.

X-Successful-Record.description:
Number of IP addresses that returned abuse contact data in this bulk
request. Entries returned as a `message` object are not counted. This
header is included only when this number is lower than the number of
submitted entries.

abuse.name: IRT-APNICRANDNET-AU
abuse.address: PO Box 3646, South Brisbane, QLD 4101, Australia

application/xml.example:
<ArrayList>
  <item>
    <ip>1.0.0.0</ip>
    <abuse>
        <route>1.0.0.0/24</route>
        <country>AU</country>
        <name>IRT-APNICRANDNET-AU</name>
        <organization></organization>
        <kind>group</kind>
        <address>PO Box 3646, South Brisbane, QLD 4101, Australia</address>
        <emails>helpdesk@apnic.net</emails>
        <phone_numbers>+61738583100</phone_numbers>
    </abuse>
  </item>
  <item>
      <message>'10.0.0.1' is a bogon IP address.</message>
  </item>
</ArrayList>

Ip.name: ip
Ip.description:
An IPv4 address or IPv6 address to look up. When omitted, the API
resolves the public IP of the requesting client. Empty or whitespace-only values
are treated the same as omission and resolve caller IP. Pass `ip` only once. If multiple `ip` query parameters are sent,
values may be merged and treated as invalid input (HTTP 400).

Fields.name: fields
Fields.description:
Comma-separated list of fields or objects to return. Everything else is omitted.
The `ip` field is always returned regardless of this filter.

Supports dot-notation for nested fields: `abuse.route`, `abuse.organization`.

If the same field or object is listed in both `fields` and `excludes`, `excludes`
wins and it is left out of the response (e.g.
`fields=abuse.name&excludes=abuse.name` drops `name`). An object left with no fields
is removed, so `fields=abuse&excludes=abuse` returns only `ip`.

If you list both an object key and one of its nested fields separated by comma
(e.g. `abuse,abuse.name`), the full object is returned.

Unknown names are ignored and the API still returns HTTP 200. Names are
case-sensitive. If none of the names in `fields` is valid, `fields` is ignored
and the full response is returned (and charged). `*` anywhere in `fields`
returns everything.

This parameter only has an effect once a request is authorized; the IP Abuse
Contact API as a whole requires a paid plan (see Plan Availability and Usage
Limits above).

none.summary: Return the full response (no field filtering)

Excludes.name: excludes
Excludes.description:
Comma-separated list of fields or objects to remove from the response. The `ip`
field cannot be excluded.

Supports dot-notation for nested fields: `abuse.name`.

If the same field or object is listed in both `fields` and `excludes`, `excludes`
wins and it is left out of the response (e.g.
`fields=abuse.name&excludes=abuse.name` drops `name`). An object left with no fields
is removed, so `fields=abuse&excludes=abuse` returns only `ip`.

Unknown fields or object keys in `excludes` are ignored. The API still returns
HTTP 200.

This parameter only has an effect once a request is authorized; the IP Abuse
Contact API as a whole requires a paid plan (see Plan Availability and Usage
Limits above).

Output.name: output
Output.description:
Desired response format. Defaults to `json` if not specified. You can also
control the format using the `Accept` header (`application/json`,
`application/xml`, or `text/xml`). For successful responses and authentication
errors, the `Accept` header takes precedence if both are provided: `output` is
used only when the `Accept` header is absent or set to `*/*`, and an `Accept`
value other than `application/xml` or `text/xml` (for example a browser's
default) returns JSON even with `output=xml`. Values are matched exactly (use
lowercase `xml`).

If `output` is unknown or unsupported, it is ignored and the response defaults
to JSON (`application/json`) with HTTP 200.

BadRequest.description:
Bad request. Returned for one of the following reasons:
- The provided IPv4 address or IPv6 address is invalid.
- Special characters such as [ ] { } | ^ ` are present in the API URL,
  either in a parameter name or its value (especially in the API key).

value.message: Provided IP address '999.999.999.999' is not valid.

specialCharacters.summary: Special characters in API URL or key

value.message: Invalid character found in the request target.

Unauthorized.description:
Unauthorized. Returned for one of the following reasons:

- An API key is required for this request, but the `apiKey` query parameter is missing and the request doesn't come from a domain added under Request Origin.
- An invalid (random or incorrect) API key is provided, or the request has no API key and its `Origin` or `Referer` domain is not registered as a Request Origin.
- The account's email address has not been verified.
- The account has been locked due to abuse or illegal activity.
- The API request is made using an API key for a database subscription.
- The API request is made using a free subscription API key.
- The subscription is in a 'paused' state.
- The subscription trial has expired.

BadRequestBulk.description:
Bad request. Returned for the whole request only when the body is missing or not
valid JSON, `ips` is missing, is not a JSON array, or is empty, or `ips` has more
than 50,000 entries, or when special characters such as [ ] { } | ^ ` are
present in the API URL, either in a parameter name or its value (especially in
the API key). An invalid IP does not fail the request: that entry is returned as
a `message` object inside the HTTP 200 array.

NotFound.description:
Not found. Returned for one of the following reasons:

- A syntactically valid IPv4 or IPv6 address does not exist in the IPGeolocation database.
- An IPv4 address or IPv6 address is passed as a path variable
  instead of as a URL query parameter (e.g., using `/v3/abuse/8.8.8.8`
  instead of `/v3/abuse?ip=8.8.8.8`).
- A non-existent or incorrect API endpoint is called.

Invalid or malformed IPv4, IPv6, or domain input returns HTTP 400 instead.

value.message: Provided IP Address 'IP_ADDRESS' doesn't exist in our database.

ipAsPathVariable.summary: IP passed as path variable instead of query parameter

value.message: No endpoint GET /v3/abuse/8.8.8.8.
No endpoint GET /v3/abuse-invalid.

MethodNotAllowed.description:
Method Not Allowed. Returned when an unsupported HTTP method is used
to call an endpoint.

Only GET and POST methods are supported:

- `GET` is allowed for the `abuse` endpoint.
- `POST` is allowed for the `abuse-bulk` endpoint.

Calling an endpoint with an HTTP method it doesn't support (for example `PUT` or `DELETE`), or using the correct method on
the wrong endpoint, results in HTTP 405.

value.message: Request method 'GET' is not supported

postNotAllowedForSingle.summary: POST used on single lookup endpoint

value.message: Request method 'POST' is not supported
Request method 'PUT' is not supported

PayloadTooLarge.description:
Payload too large. Returned by the edge proxy (nginx) when raw POST body size
exceeds configured limits before the request reaches the application.

This status is based on payload byte size, not on the number of IP entries. It
can occur even when `ips` contains only one very large value.

If both conditions apply (oversized body and `ips` count > 50,000), HTTP 413 may
be returned first because edge validation runs before application-level checks.

text/html.example:
413 Request Entity Too Large

nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu)

UnsupportedMediaType.description: Unsupported media type. The `Content-Type` header is not set to `application/json`.

Locked.description:
Locked. The provided IP address belongs to a bogon IP range or a private
network and cannot be looked up.

TooManyRequests.description:
Too Many Requests. Returned for one of the following reasons:
- The API credit allowance has been reached for an active trial subscription (capped at 100,000 API credits).
- The API credit allowance has been reached for a Paid subscription with surcharge usage disabled.
- The API credit allowance has been reached for a Paid subscription with status 'past due' or 'deleted'.
- The surcharge (overage) credit limit has been reached for the subscribed plan.

ClientClosedRequest.description:
The client closed the connection before the server finished processing the
request (logged by the edge proxy; the client receives no response). This
usually happens when the client sets a very short request or connection
timeout. Increase the timeout on the client side.

InternalServerError.description:
Internal Server Error. The server encountered an unexpected condition
that prevented it from fulfilling the request. If the issue persists,
contact support@ipgeolocation.io.

example.message: Something went wrong while processing your request. Please try again or contact technical support at support@ipgeolocation.io

BadGateway.description:
Bad Gateway. Returned by the edge proxy in front of the API, not by the API
application, when it gets an invalid response from the API server. The
response body is set by the proxy. This is usually temporary; retry the
request.

ServiceUnavailable.description:
Service Unavailable. Returned when the API cannot verify your API key (or request
origin) because of a temporary internal error, for example when the billing
service is unreachable and the key has not been verified recently. Keys that
were verified recently keep working. Retry later; if it persists, contact
support@ipgeolocation.io.

example.message: We're unable to verify your API key (YOUR_API_KEY) due to an internal error. Please contact technical support for assistance at support@ipgeolocation.io

GatewayTimeout.description:
Gateway Timeout. Returned by the edge proxy in front of the API, not by the
API application, when the API server does not respond in time. The response
body is set by the proxy. Retry the request.

HttpVersionNotSupported.description:
HTTP Version Not Supported. Returned by the edge proxy in front of the API,
not by the API application, when the request uses an HTTP protocol version
it does not support. The response body is set by the proxy.

PaymentRequired.description:
Payment Required. Returned for a paid (non-Free) subscription whose active-until
date has passed: one day after the active-until date for active or trialing
subscriptions, and from the active-until date for past-due or deleted
subscriptions. It is checked before any usage quota. Paused subscriptions and
expired trials get HTTP 401 instead, and Free plan keys never get 402. Renew or
upgrade the plan to continue using IPGeolocation API.

value.message: Your subscription has expired at 2026-01-15 00:00. Please subscribe to a paid plan to continue using IPGeolocation API without interruption or contact technical support for assistance at support@ipgeolocation.io

Forbidden.description: Forbidden. The API key has an IP allow-list and the request comes from an IP address that is not on it.

example.message: Your IP address '203.0.113.10' is not allowed to use this API key. Please contact technical support for assistance at support@ipgeolocation.io

ErrorResponse.description:
Returned for any non-200 response. Contains only a human-readable `message`.
Message text can vary by status and condition; examples in this spec are
representative, not exhaustive, and should not be treated as stable machine
codes.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of what went wrong. Use HTTP status for control flow.
message.example: Provided IP address '999.999.999.999' is not valid.

BulkAbuseRequest.description:
Request body for the bulk abuse contact lookup. Contains a single `ips` field
with an array of IP addresses to look up.

ips.description:
Array of IPv4 addresses or IPv6 addresses to look up.
Must not be empty. Maximum 50,000 entries per request. Each entry is
resolved independently, so you can mix IPv4 and IPv6 freely.

BulkAbuseResponseItem.description:
A single element in the bulk lookup response array. Each element is either a
full abuse contact lookup object or an error object containing only `message`.

ip.description: IP address for this lookup result.

BulkAbuseErrorItem.description:
Error object returned for an entry in the bulk lookup request that has no abuse
contact data (invalid, empty, null, private or bogon IP, or an IP with no abuse
contact in the database). Contains only a `message` field. Note: unlike success
entries, error entries do NOT include the original `ip` field, so the only way to
correlate errors to inputs is by array index. The response array preserves the
same order as the request `ips` array.

message.description: Human-readable error for the specific bulk entry.
message.example: Provided IP address 'invalid-ip' is not valid.

AbuseLookupResponse.description:
Response returned by the IP Abuse Contact API.

Contains the queried IP address and the abuse contact information
associated with the network responsible for that IP.

The `ip` field is always present. The `abuse` object may be partially
populated depending on available registry data and field filtering.

ip.description: The IP address for which abuse contact details are returned.

Abuse.description: Abuse contact information for the network that owns this IP. Costs 1 credit.

route.description: BGP route prefix this abuse contact is responsible for, in CIDR notation.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the abuse contact. May be empty.

name.description: Name of the abuse contact person or team.

organization.description: Organization name of the abuse contact. May be empty.

kind.description: Contact type from registry data. Values include `group`, `individual`.

address.description: Postal address of the abuse contact. Returned as a plain comma-separated string.
address.example: Tele2 AB/Swedish IP Network, IP Registry, Torshamnsgatan 17 164 40 Kista SWEDEN

phone_numbers.description: Phone numbers for the abuse contact.

ApiKeyAuth.name: apiKey
ApiKeyAuth.description:
API key passed as the `apiKey` query parameter. Get yours from the
[IPGeolocation dashboard](https://app.ipgeolocation.io/). For client-side
usage, consider using Request Origin (CORS) authentication instead to
avoid exposing your key.

tags.name: IP Abuse Contact
tags.description:
API endpoints for retrieving abuse contact information associated
with IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. The response contains registry-based
contact details for reporting malicious or abusive network activity
such as spam, phishing, DDoS attacks, or unauthorized access attempts.

The single lookup endpoint (`GET /v3/abuse`) returns one IP per
request.

The bulk lookup endpoint (`POST /v3/abuse-bulk`) accepts up to
50,000 IP addresses per request.
